pr_title: w32_common: refactor and improve window state handling
pr_body:
Refactored `reinit_window_state` function:
Moved all the code related to fitting window on screen in a separate function `fit_window_on_screen`.
Also simplified that code a lot to make it easier to read and added a few debug messages.

Fixed #4753 by disabling the above mensioned code in `fit_window_on_screen` for a maximized window, since maximized window should already fit on the screen just fine.
It should be noted that this bug was only reproducible with `--fit-border` option which is enabled by default. The cause of the bug is that after calling the `add_window_borders` for a maximized window, the rect in result is slightly larger than the screen rect, which is okay, `SetWindowPos` will interpret it as a maximized state later, so no auto-fitting to screen size is needed here.

In `reinit_window_state` debug message `reset window bounds` now reports client area size and position, instead of window area size and position. This is done for consistency with debug messages in handling
fullscreen state above in this function, since they also print window bounds of the client area.

All in all, the `reinit_window_state` is much shorter now.
pr_comments:
Tested this patch. After returned from first fullscreen, if I try to enter fullscreen again, this happened.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9623615/33801876-45a85efc-dda4-11e7-8256-a2d83c6e3b60.png)

@shinchiro, thanks, fixed.

`SetWindowLongPtrW` sometimes triggers `WM_SIZE` event, which updates the `w32->dw` and `w32->dh` values, so they should be saved beforehand.
Oops, forgot to move the changed size and pos from rect back to `w32` struct. Updated again.

Updated.

Added a commit fixing #5215 - always try to fit to virtual screen instead of the active screen. If there is only one monitor, the behavior will stay the same as it was before this change.

Added a commit fixing #2451 - that was an easy fix, just moved the `ITaskbarList2_MarkFullscreenWindow` below the `SetWindowPos`, so the taskbar is notified after the window is shown. So there's no need to create and show the window in normal mode before switching to fullscreen.

Looks good. ``fit_window_on_screen`` is definitely clearer than the old logic. I'm not sure using the virtual screen size is the best solution to #5215 though, since it also affects the window size when loading new files.
Just for the reference, this function doesn't affect `autofit` options in any way, so it shouldn't have any side effects.

Using virtual screen size is the only way to fix #5215 , I believe, because `reinit_window_state` is called not only when switching fullscreen state, but on other events as well, like toggling border or ontop options. So skipping `fit_window_on_screen` on leaving fullscreen is not an option, and doing this is going to bring inconsistency to mpv window behavior.

There is definitely one side-effect. If you don't use --autofit and you open a file that's larger than the current monitor, mpv will size the window to the virtual screen with these patches. Without the patch, it sizes the window to the current monitor.

I do think #5215 is a valid bug, but maybe it's better solved by skipping the ``fit_window_on_screen`` logic in some cases. It definitely seems odd that ``fit_window_on_screen`` is applied when toggling ontop.

> Without the patch, it sizes the window to the current monitor.

The question is, does the user on a multi-monitor system really expect this behavior? What if someone has 9 screens as a one huge monitor (3x3) and doesn't want to use `--fs-screen=all` for some reason?

At least this should be optional I think, like I've already suggested in the issue #5215 
I don't like the idea of skipping this function, because in this case Windows will handle unusual window sizes anyway, and it might contradict with `--fit-border` option.

> The question is, does the user on a multi-monitor system really expect this behavior? 

I think so. I think the common case is to have a pair of monitors, a primary monitor and auxiliary monitor or some other device like a TV or a projector. You don't really want programs to decide to span multiple-monitors of their own accord with these setups, since it's annoying to have to size them back down to the monitor you are using, especially if it sizes the window back up when opening new files, and especially if the monitors aren't actually next to each other, like with a projector setup.

It seems like this is trading one strange behaviour (mpv restoring to a different size when leaving fullscreen) with another (mpv spanning multiple monitors on startup.) But the simple way to make mpv restore to the same size after leaving fullscreen is to skip the fit-to-screen logic. It's odd for something like toggling fullscreen (or toggling ontop) to change the user-specified window size. Toggling fullscreen should work like toggling maximize. (We could use Get/SetWindowPlacement for this.)

There's another issue (#2202) which could benefit from using `Get/SetWindowPlacement`, I planned to address this problem a bit later, to not make a mess out of this PR.

I agree with you, that this is expected behavior for a user with dual-screen setup. I'll see what can be done with this when I get home.

Ah great, thanks. I've been meaning to use Get/SetWindowPlacement for fullscreen toggling for a while but I never got around to it.

> I planned to address this problem a bit later, to not make a mess out of this PR.

I don't mind too much either way, but it might be an idea to split this PR then. 84b360f and d9bb32b look good IMO. (I'm definitely happy about the ``fit_window_on_screen`` refactoring.)

Updated. Please read the commit messages.

I'm using `RECT` now for storing screen and window size & pos, since it's much easier to use them this way in WinAPI functions.
Split the `fit_window_on_screen` into two functions: `fit_rect` is a helper function to fit one rect on another.

Splitting the `reinit_window_state` into 4 functions allowed to skip the certain parts on updating the `ontop` and `border` properties.

I'm skipping the `fit_window_on_screen` when toggling fullscreen, so the issue we discussed above is fixed now without using the virtual screen size.

Found another minor issue: since the `fit_window_on_screen` was skipped on leaving fullscreen, when a new video file was opened (via drag-n-drop) while the window was in fullscreen, the `fit_window_on_screen` wasn't called to adjust the new window size.

Fixed it by adding a new flag `fit_on_screen`. When this flag is set, the `fit_window_on_screen` will be called even when leaving fullscreen. I set this flag in `gui_thread_reconfig` on window initialization and when the video size was reset.

Refactored `gui_thread_reconfig` according to my recent window RECT changes.
Looks fine as far as I can tell, except for a couple of minor issues that I commented on. I like that it's using RECT now, since it simplifies a lot of code.

issue_context.title: Leaving fullscreen doesn't properly maximize mpv window again if taskbar is docked to Right or Left
issue_context.body:
### mpv version and platform

0.26.0, Windows 7 SP1

### Reproduction steps
Go to "Taskbar and Start Menu Properties" and set your Windows taskbar location on screen to Left or Right (won't reproduce if set to Bottom or Top).
Run mpv.
Maximize the mpv window.
Go to fullscreen mode.
Exit fullscreen mode.
### Expected behavior
The window should return to maximized state, covering all available area.
### Actual behavior
The window is "maximized" (can't be maximized, but can be restored), but its position doesn't cover all available area anymore. Here's a screenshot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21028464/29240271-1dc072e4-7f7b-11e7-8b69-363f0c0ddb7c.png)

### Log file

https://pastebin.com/z6qewecF

review_comments: Fine for now, but in future it might be better to solve this by applying the fit-on-screen logic to prev_windowrc when it's updated.

Maybe, but it'll require storing the virtual screen size in a separate RECT, e.g. `vscreenrc`, instead of `screenrc`, for the case when `--fs-screen=all` is set. I still think that the fit on screen logic should stay as it is now, to make sure the window styles are up to date at the moment of adjusting the window bounds.
